entities.summary: Gratian was a Roman Emperor and Magister Militum (400 CE – 407 CE), recognized as a landmark figure in the Classical era. Born in Rome (Italia, Global), they rose to power after the death of Emperor Valentinian II and ruled jointly with his half-brother Valentinian III. Gratian's reign was marked by significant military campaigns, including the Battle of Frigidus, where they defeated the Visigoths and expanded the Roman Empire's borders. His policies also led to the establishment of the Salian Merovingian dynasty, which would shape Western European history for centuries to come. Gratian's legacy is still studied by historians today, who seek to understand the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the late Roman Empire. As the Roman Empire's military power began to wane, Gratian's leadership was crucial in maintaining the empire's territorial integrity. Despite his significant achievements, Gratian's reign was cut short by his death in 407 CE, which marked the beginning of a period of fragmentation and decline for the Western Roman Empire.
